The project intends to help public institutions mitigate corruption & integrity risks, strengthen ethics and integrity of target institutions from all three branches of powers including independent institutions. It will do so by supporting the selected public institutions to put in place a coherent and effective integrity system and promoting of integrity management practices at the institutional level with the end objective to improve the level of transparency and accountability of public institutions towards citizens.

The project targets the nexus between public trust, citizens engagement, institutional accountability and integrity through a collaborative process and instruments of integrity management system. The ultimate goal is to regain citizens as a cornerstone and key ally of institutions in their efforts to deliver integrity governance.
The objectives of the intervention are: - Institutional capacities in target institutions are built for the development and adoption of integrity plans . - Capacities of civil players are built to improve implementation of institutional integrity plans through monitoring and evidence-based feedback.

The most significant results of the intervention are assessed as following: - All six partnerer institutions (Parliament of Albania, High Prosecutorial Council, Commissioner for the Right of Information and Data Protection, Ministry of Health and Social Protection, Institute of Public health, General Directorate of Taxes) formally approved Integrity?Plans (from zero at baseline) and six created fully operational Institutional Working Groups (IWGs) that update risk registers at least quarterly. - Four Civil Society Organization (CSO) expert teams completed the inaugural Integrity?Index cycle, issuing 120? recommendations85?% already taken up in official action plans and 60?% implemented. - Enabling instruments were institutionalized: Department of Public Administration (DoPAs) ethics package is mandatory across the civil service Albanian School of Public Administration (ASPA) hosts a 12hour ethics module with 150 certified trainees Albanian State Audit Institution (ALSAI) will pilot integrity focused audits in 2025.
The intervention revolved around three mutually reinforcing pillars: - Integrity Working Groups (IWGs) in each partner trained in the Integrity RiskAssessment (IRA) methodology and tasked with drafting risk based Integrity Plans; - Civic Monitoring Framework (CiMoF) later rebranded the Integrity?Index of Public Institutions that enables CSOs to rate implementation and publish independent scorecards. - Knowledge & systems support, including a national Ethics Manual, a practical IRA guide, socialexperiment research, an elearning curriculum and the first integrity audit methodology for the State Audit Institution.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
